prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: In frames 1–2, the depth map captures a top-down view where the camera wearer's right arm and hand-held plastic piping bag protrude forward from the bottom-right at roughly 0.3 to 0.6 m (rising closer in frame 2), suspended above flat wooden pattern boards and ground surfaces about 0.8 to 1.1 m below. As the camera turns left in frames 3–5, bright foreground regions show the wearer's own bent knees and right arm at the bottom (0.2 to 0.5 m away) and a second person standing immediately to the front-left at 0.4 to 0.8 m, separated by about 0.3 to 0.5 m from the raised boards on the right and standing over a floor with sacks and metal basins at 1.0 to 1.3 m depth. In frame 5, the wearer's left arm reaches out at 0.3 to 0.6 m to make contact with the standing person's upper back, placing both the piping bag, the nearby boards, and the second person within arm's reach while both bodies remain partially out of view at the frame borders and the second person faces downward away from the camera. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the elevated foreground limbs, the standing person's torso, and the stepped height of the wooden boards from the cluttered floor background. However, it is unreliable where the standing person's blue trousers and the floor in frames 3–4 drop into overly dark, deep-looking voids, and where fine 3D relief on the piped leaf patterns is flattened in frame 2.
descriptions.segmentation: The instance segmentation map partitions the top-down workspace and people across the five frames, showing the flat pattern board in frame 1 (~0.8 to 1.0 m below the camera), the wearer's extended right arm and held plastic bag within arm's reach (~0.3 to 0.6 m) in frame 2, and the transition in frames 3–5 to the wearer's lower body at the bottom (~0.2 to 0.5 m) alongside the second person standing to the front-left (~0.4 to 0.8 m away). Across frames 3–5, the standing person remains oriented away from the camera wearer with their head cropped out of the upper frame edge, positioned just left of the pattern boards (~0.3 to 0.5 m apart) and above the floor-level sacks and metal basins (~1.0 to 1.3 m away), before the wearer's left arm bridges the gap in frame 5 to touch the standing person's back. While the masks help isolate contiguous regions such as the wearer's reaching arm in frame 2, the wearer's seated lap in frames 3–4, and a metal basin on the left floor in frame 5 from the busy background textures, the semantic labels and boundaries are highly unreliable. Specifically, the map misclassifies the ground board as a 'bed' (wholly omitting the wearer's arm in frame 1), labels the plastic piping bag an 'umbrella', labels the standing person a 'fire hydrant' in frame 3, and calls the floor basin a 'cup' in frame 5. It also completely misses the background boards in frames 2–5 and merges the wearer's reaching left arm with the second person's torso into a single overlapping 'person' mask in frame 5.
descriptions.pose: Across all five frames, the pose map is completely blank (solid black), failing to detect any body skeletons or hand keypoints for either the camera wearer or the second person. In the RGB strip, the camera wearer's right arm and hand are clearly visible in the foreground (~0.3 to 0.6 m away, within arm's reach of the pattern boards in frames 1–2 and resting near the wearer's knees at ~0.2 to 0.5 m in frames 3–4), and the wearer's left arm reaches out in frame 5 (~0.3 to 0.6 m) to touch the back of the standing person positioned ~0.4 to 0.8 m to the front-left. Because the egocentric viewpoint looks steeply downward (~0.8 to 1.3 m to the boards and floor), both individuals suffer from severe truncation and self-occlusion, with only detached limbs and lower torso visible for the wearer and only the top-down back, shoulders, and lower legs visible for the standing person facing away from the camera. Consequently, the pose map provides no spatial information beyond what is in the RGB image and is entirely unreliable under these steep top-down angles and heavy frame-edge occlusions.
